newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African arms manufacturer steps up exports.
newsitem.headline: S.African arms manufacturer steps up exports.

text.p: South African state-owned arms manufacturer Denel could earn between 15 and 20 billion rand from exports over the next five years, Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said on Monday.
Opening the debate on her 1997/98 budget, Sigcau said that Denel had invested up to 100 million rand a year in new product development and technology upgrading.

"Although Denel is considered a large company in the context of the South African industry, with exports exceeding one billion rand in 1995/96, it is but a small player in global terms, ranking as the 65th largest manufacturer of defence equipment," she said.
But it had established itself as a reliable supplier of quality products in global niche markets and exports would help it develop its technology further and maintain world class competitiveness.
Denel had also examined new markets at home and abroad and sales to the mining industry had risen to 35 million rand in 1996/97 from seven million rand in 1994/95.
"Exciting new mining products and systems are currently under development," she said.
These included a new rock breaking device and emergency medical equipment.

Denel's aviation division had formed a strategic alliance with the French-German helicopter manufacturer, Eurocopter, aimed at strengthening co-operation on the Rooivalk attack helicopter and Oryx medium transport helicopter programmes.
"Co-operation will focus on development, production and customer support for these two products," she said.
"Joint international marketing of these helicopters may also be considered as the companies have complementary product lines.
"Both Denel and Eurocopter are convinced that joint co-operation will significantly enhance their position in today's highly competitive global defence market."
She said that Denel had several other joint venture partnerships which had to be taken into considation in any plans to restructure the corporation.
